sources.label: TS SDK Workflow message passing (handler drain, signal acceptance, errors)
sources.summary: Official TS guidance: await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished) before return/CAN; signal() returns on server acceptance, NOT handler delivery; TMPRL1102 warning on unfinished handlers; WorkflowNotFoundError when workflow does not exist; gRPC NOT_FOUND (code 5) when workflow finished while handler in progress.

sources.label: Handling Signals, Queries, & Updates (cross-SDK)
sources.summary: Canonical guidance to await All-Handlers-Finished condition before run completion or CAN; HandlerUnfinishedPolicy.ABANDON to silence warnings; clients waiting on Updates get Not Found if Updates never complete.

sources.label: TS SDK API: Namespace workflow (allHandlersFinished)
sources.summary: allHandlersFinished() returns true iff no in-progress update or signal handler executions; intended to be awaited via workflow.condition before return/CAN to prevent handler interruption.

sources.label: TS SDK API: WorkflowHandle (signal/result/terminate/cancel)
sources.summary: signal() = Signal a running Workflow (resolves on acceptance); result() = Promise that resolves when Workflow execution completes; terminate() = Terminate a running Workflow; cancel() triggers CancelledFailure in root scope and propagates to Activities/Child Workflows per cancellationType.

sources.label: TS SDK API: WorkflowClient (result follows chain)
sources.summary: result(): 'Get the result of a Workflow execution. Follow the chain of execution in case Workflow continues as new, or has a cron schedule or retry policy.' getHandle does not validate workflowId; missing workflow -> WorkflowNotFoundError from describe().

sources.label: TS SDK source: workflow-client.ts (signal/describe RPCs)
sources.summary: signal() composes interceptors over _signalWorkflowHandler (SignalWorkflowExecution RPC) and returns void; describe() is direct DescribeWorkflowExecution RPC returning raw proto. Confirms acceptance-vs-execution split.

sources.label: TS SDK source: errors.ts (full client error catalog - NO WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError)
sources.summary: Client error classes: ServiceError, WorkflowFailedError (result on failure), WorkflowContinuedAsNewError (CAN with followRuns=false), WorkflowUpdateFailedError, WorkflowUpdateRPCTimeoutOrCancelledError. NO WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError exists in the TS SDK; that name is Cadence/Java only. WorkflowNotFoundError comes from @temporalio/common.

sources.label: TS SDK source: workflow.ts (allHandlersFinished impl)
sources.summary: allHandlersFinished() returns activator.inProgressSignals.size === 0 && activator.inProgressUpdates.size === 0. Pure in-flight counter; does NOT await Activities started inside handlers, does NOT block future signal acceptance.

sources.label: TS SDK source: internals.ts (TMPRL1102 warning)
sources.summary: When a signal handler is still running asynchronously at workflow main-function completion, the WFT does NOT fail; completeWorkflowExecution is still sent, a TMPRL1102 warning is emitted, and the handler is abandoned/interrupted. Suppressed via HandlerUnfinishedPolicy.ABANDON.

sources.label: PR #1459 (allHandlersFinished introduction)
sources.summary: Adds allHandlersFinished() and the unfinished-handler warning (default on, except on cancellation/failure). Documents the dangling-handler footgun the API addresses.

sources.label: Visibility (eventual consistency, authoritative single-entity reads)
sources.summary: Visibility is an async-updated search index with variable propagation lag (seconds or longer); no SLA; treat as eventually consistent. Single-entity lookups (DescribeWorkflowExecution, DescribeSchedule) bypass Visibility and are authoritative. Visibility is for search/filter/count, not for reading current state of one execution.

sources.label: Cancel a Workflow - TypeScript SDK
sources.summary: Cancellation semantics in TS: root scope throws CancelledFailure('Workflow canceled'); cancellation propagates to Activities/Child Workflows per cancellationType; cleanup must run in CancellationScope.nonCancellable; cancellation is cooperative, not immediate. Reset section notes reset 'terminates the current Workflow Execution'.

sources.label: Activity Execution (cancellation, async completion)
sources.summary: Activity cancellation lets the Activity clean up; Activities must heartbeat to receive cancellation; Activity receives CancelledFailure with message 'NOT_FOUND' when Workflow Run reached a Closed state. Asynchronous Activity Completion vs Signal tradeoffs.

sources.label: References: Commands (CancelWorkflowExecution)
sources.summary: CancelWorkflowExecution Command is triggered only AFTER the Workflow has successfully cleaned up following a Cancellation Request; its event is one of the few that can be last in an Event History. Confirms cancellation requires workflow code to run.

sources.label: Interrupt a Workflow - Cancellation and Termination (official overview)
sources.summary: Cancellation = graceful, lets workflow clean up; Termination = immediate, for stuck workflows. Authoritative framing of the two interrupt mechanisms.

sources.label: Versioning - TypeScript SDK (patched/deprecatePatch)
sources.summary: Three-step patching: (1) patched('id') inserts a marker, runs new code on new runs, old code on in-flight; (2) deprecatePatch('id') once old runs gone (marker tolerated on replay); (3) remove both once pre-patch runs leave retention. Adding/removing/reordering awaits on Activities changes command sequence and requires versioning. Worker Versioning is the alternative: Pinned workflows run on a single Deployment Version and need no patching.

sources.label: Worker Versioning (Build IDs, Pinned vs Auto-Upgrade)
sources.summary: Pinned Workflows complete on a single Worker Deployment Version and don't need patching. Auto-Upgrade Workflows move to new code on rollout and must be kept replay-safe manually (i.e. with patching). Use temporal workflow update-options to move a pinned workflow to a new version.

sources.label: Continue-As-New - TypeScript SDK
sources.summary: CAN closes the current run successfully and starts a new run in the same chain with a fresh Event History. Do NOT call CAN from handlers; wait for allHandlersFinished first in the main workflow. Use when approaching Event History limits (wf.workflowInfo().continueAsNewSuggested).

sources.label: External Storage (payload lifecycle beyond retention)
sources.summary: External storage must retain payloads for the full Workflow lifetime PLUS the Namespace retention period. TTL must cover Workflow lifetime + retention window. For indefinite workflows, use Continue-as-New so old-run payloads only need to survive through their retention period. Temporal does NOT auto-delete payloads from external stores.

sources.label: Event History (limits, replay, Side Effects)
sources.summary: Event History is durably persisted and is the source of truth for Durable Execution and replay. Warning at 10,240 events; CAN to avoid limits. Side Effect result is recorded once and not re-executed on replay; never use Side Effect for code that could fail - use an Activity.

sources.label: Idempotency blog (Activity at-least-once, replay skips re-execution)
sources.summary: Activities are at-least-once; Activity inputs/outputs are stored in history and replayed from history (NOT re-executed) on replay. State that an Activity stores internally is lost on replay. Therefore state required beyond history must be written to an external store from inside the Activity.

sources.label: Non-retryable errors design pattern (RetryPolicy.maximumAttempts)
sources.summary: TS RetryPolicy example: retry: { nonRetryableErrorTypes: [...] } and retry: { maximumAttempts: N }. Documents maximumAttempts as the bound on Activity retries.

sources.label: Robust message handlers blog (dangling handlers)
sources.summary: Dangling handlers (left partially finished when Workflow completes/CAN) cause data inconsistency and unmet client expectations; All-Handlers-Finished + Handler Unfinished Policy address this.

sources.label: Community: race condition signal handler vs workflow completion (official recommendation)
sources.summary: Once the workflow function returns the workflow is completed and all its activities are considered canceled thus not retried. Official recommendation: await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished). Confirms the Activity-in-handler + early-return footgun.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The TypeScript SDK documents a single canonical terminal pattern that satisfies all four hard constraints (durable external write, applied-proof, handler drain, post-retention survival): the workflow main function awaits an Activity that durably writes the archived state to the external store, then awaits wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished), then returns normally. Natural return produces WorkflowExecutionCompleted. terminate() is rejected: it is server-side, immediate, runs no workflow code, performs no handler drain, and writes no final Activity. cancel() is rejected: it is cooperative-abort semantics resulting in WorkflowExecutionCanceled, not an archived terminal; it is the wrong closing status. Completion proof must come from handle.result() (which blocks to terminal close and throws WorkflowFailedError/WorkflowContinuedAsNewError/WorkflowNotFoundError) or handle.describe() (single-entity, bypasses Visibility, authoritative) - NOT from signal() (acceptance-only) and NOT from Visibility (eventually consistent, no SLA, not for single-execution state). State beyond retention MUST be written from an Activity to an external store; history is deleted at retention expiry and replayed Activities are not re-executed. Adding the terminal Activity changes the command sequence for in-flight workflows, requiring either the patched()/deprecatePatch() three-step or Worker Versioning with Pinned workflows; Continue-as-New rotation only avoids patching if the workflow naturally rotates before the next terminal transition. Idempotency: the TS SDK has NO WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError class (Cadence/Java only); signalling an already-completed/closed workflow surfaces as WorkflowNotFoundError (gRPC NOT_FOUND), which the caller must disambiguate against wrong-ID/never-existed/retention-deleted via describe() before treating as idempotency evidence.

validation.notes: Docs give a clear, single correct terminal-action shape satisfying all four constraints. No documentation gap blocks the architecture decision. Two operational risks remain (see tradeoffs) but neither is a docs-level blocker: (1) NOT_FOUND disambiguation on the archive signal, (2) patching/Worker-Versioning discipline for in-flight workflows when adding the terminal Activity.

tradeoffs: Adding an Activity to the terminal path changes the command sequence and forces patching()/deprecatePatch() discipline OR Worker Versioning with Pinned workflows for safe rollout of in-flight executions.
handle.result() blocks the caller until terminal close; if the workflow is long-running or stuck, the caller holds a long-lived RPC (mitigate with describe() status polling or a result() deadline).

allHandlersFinished() is a point-in-time in-flight counter: it does NOT prevent a signal from being accepted in the microsecond between the condition resolving and the workflow returning, and it does NOT await Activities started inside handlers - the workflow author must await those explicitly.

WorkflowNotFoundError (gRPC NOT_FOUND) on the archive signal is ambiguous across already-completed / never-existed / retention-deleted; the caller needs an extra describe() round-trip to disambiguate before treating it as idempotency evidence.
Durable external write requires the external store's TTL to cover Workflow lifetime + Namespace retention; Temporal does not auto-clean external payloads.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Server-side immediate stop; runs no workflow code; performs no handler drain; writes no final Activity; closing event is WorkflowExecutionTerminated, not Completed. Fails the durable-write and handler-drain constraints. docs.temporal.io/evaluate/.../interrupt-workflow frames termination as the stuck-workflow escape hatch, not a planned terminal.

Cooperative cancellation produces WorkflowExecutionCanceled closing status (abort semantics), not an archived terminal. Even with cleanup in CancellationScope.nonCancellable, the closing event is wrong for an archive transition. docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/cancellation and references/commands confirm cancel requires workflow cleanup code to run and yields Canceled.

FORBIDDEN by the hard constraint (defineUpdate not allowed in workflow-reachable code). Also, Update acceptance (ADMITTED/ACCEPTED) is not application-level proof; only COMPLETED is, and COMPLETED still does not prove the external write was applied unless the Update handler itself awaits the Activity - which is the same drain problem signals have.

docs.temporal.io/visibility states Visibility is an async-updated search index with variable lag, no SLA, and explicitly NOT for reading the current state of one execution. Use DescribeWorkflowExecution (single-entity, bypasses Visibility) or result() instead.

alternatives_considered.option: Worker Versioning (Pinned) instead of patching() for rollout
alternatives_considered.rationale: Pinned workflows complete on a single Worker Deployment Version and need no patching (docs.temporal.io/.../worker-versioning). Correct choice for NEW workflows registered with VersioningBehaviorPinned. Does NOT help existing in-flight Auto-Upgrade workflows, which still require patched()/deprecatePatch() to add the terminal Activity safely.

alternatives_considered.option: Wait for Continue-As-New rotation instead of patching
alternatives_considered.rationale: CAN starts a fresh run that adopts current code; if the workflow rotates regularly and the terminal transition can wait until the next rotation, patching is unnecessary for that change. Not viable for a workflow that must archive BEFORE its next scheduled CAN rotation, or one that never rotates.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt natural-completion-after-Activity-persisted-write. Pair with patched()/deprecatePatch() three-step for in-flight Auto-Upgrade workflows, or Worker Versioning Pinned for new workflows. Do NOT use terminate() or cancel() for the archive terminal.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Adopt natural-completion-after-Activity-persisted-write as the terminal action. Concrete sequence: (1) archive signal handler sets a 'terminal requested' flag and does NOT do the external write itself; (2) workflow main function observes the flag, awaits the archive Activity (which writes archived state to the external store with idempotency key = workflowId+runId), awaits wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished), then returns the archive result; (3) caller treats signal() as acceptance-only and obtains applied-proof via handle.result() (blocks to Completed) or, for an already-completed workflow, handle.describe() confirming status==Completed with the expected runId; (4) on signal() throwing WorkflowNotFoundError, run describe() to disambiguate already-completed (idempotent success) vs never-existed/retention-deleted (error); (5) roll out the new terminal Activity via patched('add-archive-activity') three-step (or register new workflows as VersioningBehaviorPinned under Worker Versioning); (6) ensure the external store TTL >= Workflow lifetime + Namespace retention. Treat WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError as non-existent in the TS SDK; the actual error is WorkflowNotFoundError (gRPC NOT_FOUND).

> Origin: `/adv-problem` triage, 2026-08-04. Defect origin — RCA required per rq-defectOriginRca01.
> RCA revised 2026-08-04T02:15Z on workflow-history evidence; Temporal-correctness obligations added 02:20Z.

## Why

ADV archive can complete its git-side work — bundle written, PR merged to the default branch — and report success while never telling the change workflow it was archived. The workflow stays `RUNNING` with `AdvChangeStatus ["draft"]` until retention deletes it.

Archived changes keep reporting `status: draft`, `phase: release`, and resurface in `/adv-cleanup` as ready-to-archive candidates. Shipped work is offered for re-archiving.

Two distinct failures compound, and fixing only the first would leave the system still broken:

1. **The archive transition is skipped** — gated on a stale projection read.
2. **Even when it fires, it is not the correct Temporal action** — the terminal path never durably persists state before the workflow completes.

The unifying pattern: **Temporal is being used as a side effect rather than as the authority.** A derived projection was given power over the workflow that produces it, and the workflow was never made responsible for the durability of its own terminal state.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Defect origin:** archive returns `success: true` while the change workflow remains `RUNNING` with `AdvChangeStatus ["draft"]`, `AdvLifecycleState ["open"]`, `AdvCurrentBucket ["in_flight"]`.

### Decisive evidence — workflow history

Full history for pokeedge-web `replaceTypedOgBrandingWordmark` (archived `2026-08-04T00:24:04Z`), 787 events:

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| `WORKFLOW_TASK_SCHEDULED` / `STARTED` / `COMPLETED` | 147 / 147 / 147 — worker alive, zero backlog, nothing unprocessed |
| `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_SIGNALED` | 139, across 21 distinct signal names |
| Archive or close signals | **ZERO. Never present in history.** |
| Last substantive signal | `adv.change.phase9StatusUpdated` @ `2026-07-27T17:23:05Z` |
| Final events | `adv.change.worktreeCreated` @ `2026-08-04T00:00:34Z`, then nothing |
| History events at archive time (`00:24:04Z`) | **none** |

This rules out the entire delivery-failure family — not accepted-then-dropped, not queued behind a dead worker, not lost to continue-as-new rotation. **It was never sent.**

### Fault 1 — precondition short-circuit (why the signal was never sent)

`plugin/src/tools/change.ts:4836-4838`:

```ts
if (!dryRun && archiveResult.success) {
  const statusAlreadyArchived = change.status === "archived";
  if (!statusAlreadyArchived) {
    // ... store.changes.save(change)  ← the ONLY call that signals the workflow
  }
}
```

`store.changes.save()` is the sole path firing `archiveConvergedSignal` / `archiveRequestedSignal` / `archiveChangeSignal` (`storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:1396-1450`). Guarding it on `change.status === "archived"` means:

1. Some earlier path writes `status: "archived"` into the **disk projection** without signalling the workflow.
2. Every subsequent archive run loads that projection, evaluates `statusAlreadyArchived === true`, and **skips the save entirely**.
3. Archive proceeds through git finalization, removes the change directory, returns `success: true`.
4. The workflow is never told. No retry can fix it — the same short-circuit fires every time. Self-perpetuating.

Corroboration on the same change: `gates.release: {status: "pending"}` and `phase9_status: {status: "pending_merge"}` despite a merged PR; last `projection_commits` revision (`2026-08-04T00:00:35Z`) **pre-dates** the archive.

The precondition treats a **projection read** as authority over a **workflow transition**. It is idempotency logic guarding the wrong thing: it asks "does the projection already say archived?" when the question is "has the workflow been told?"

### Fault 2 — the terminal path is not the correct Temporal action

Independent of Fault 1, the archive transition as currently written would still not produce durable terminal state.

| Finding | Citation |
|---|---|
| `archiveChangeSignal` handler passes `{ afterSuccess: false }`, which short-circuits `upsertSignalSearchAttributes` **and** `scheduleChangeProjection`. | `temporal/workflows.ts:2138`; `:1107-1111` |
| The handler manually re-adds the search-attribute upserts it lost — but **not** the projection write. | `temporal/workflows.ts:2119-2136` |
| The workflow's terminal path logs, drains handlers, returns. **No `writeChangeProjection` activity before completing.** | `temporal/workflows.ts:2230-2239` |
| `writeChangeProjection` exists as a proxied Activity with `retry: { maximumAttempts: 3 }` — it is simply not used on the terminal path. | `temporal/workflows.ts:218-226` |

Consequence: terminal state is written **only** by the caller, best-effort, outside any Temporal durability guarantee. The workflow completes without ever durably recording that it is terminal. Once retention expires, no evidence survives — which is why `purgeStaleDocumentation` (29h) and older changes return NOT FOUND with nothing to fall back on.

Temporal's own guidance is explicit that state which must outlive `WorkflowExecutionRetentionTtl` has to be written from an Activity to an external store; the workflow is orchestration, not the system of record (docs.temporal.io/production-deployment/self-hosted-guide/archival). The Activity exists here. It is not wired to the terminal path.

### Amplifiers — why it stayed invisible and unrecoverable

**A1 — no postcondition.** Archive never verifies the transition applied. `signal()` resolves on server-accept, not handler execution (docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing). The only readback is a `changeStateQuery` with a 5s timeout (`storage/store-temporal/gates.ts:80-85`) — a state query, never a lifecycle assertion.

**A2 — workflow never read as terminal source.** `terminalFromWorkflow: 0` is a hardcoded literal (`archive/terminal-history.ts:472`). List hydration resolves only from archive bundle (`status === "archived"`) or disk (`status === "closed"`). `show` answers from the bundle → archived; `list` answers from the stale disk row → draft. The ladders cannot agree by construction.

**A3 — reconciliation deadlock.** The veto predicate counts any change whose **disk** status is non-terminal as active and skips it (`reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:161-165`; `reconcile-terminal-deps.ts:115-123, 171-172`) — reading the same projection the defect corrupted. This explains `inspected: 91, skipped: 91, reconciled: 0, failed: 0` exactly. Candidacy is further limited to `RUNNING` Visibility rows (`:154`), so retention-expired workflows have no repair path. Doctor reports healthy because it probes infrastructure liveness, never state correctness.

**A4 — shared verifier.** Archive-convergence recovery and `bulk_close` `status_transition` share one postcondition verifier and message template (`storage/change-projection-transaction.ts:470-485`; `tools/_recovery-writers.ts:108`; `tools/change.ts:777`). `bulk_close` shows the same misleading-result symptom. Confirmed shared, not assumed.

### Supporting evidence

- **advance itself** exhibits the symptom: 54 in-flight, many `phase: release` with all tasks done.
- pokeedge-web: 206 in-flight, nearly all `completedTasks == taskCount`; ~220 affected records.
- **Reproduced live during authoring:** `adv_change_create` returned `ToolExecutionTimeout` after 10000ms; the change was created. Caller received failure for a mutation that landed — inverse of archive returning success for one that did not. Same missing-postcondition class.

### Ruled-out paths

| Considered | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| Signal accepted but never processed (dead worker / queue mismatch) | **Disproved by history.** 147/147 workflow tasks completed; zero archive signals ever present. |
| Signal lost to continue-as-new rotation | No archive signal exists in any run's history. |
| Retention TTL too short | Controls *when the symptom becomes visible*, not whether terminal state was written. Raising it hides the defect. Mitigation, tracked separately. |
| Workflow missing terminal condition | Present and correct — terminal predicate, handler drain, return (`workflows.ts:2221-2240`). The gap is the absent durable write, not the exit. |
| Missing `allHandlersFinished` drain | Present on both return paths (`:2238, :2244`). |
| Archive git-side failure | Git side succeeds — bundle committed, PR merged, verified on `origin/main`. |
| Fixing only the missing signal | Insufficient. Fault 2 means a correctly-delivered signal still yields no durable terminal state. |
| Archive-only defect | `bulk_close` shares the verifier. Mutation-durability scope. |
| Adopt Temporal Update for synchronous response | `defineUpdate` forbidden in workflow-reachable code (AGENTS.md). Signal + verified completion is the available correct pattern. |

### Spec-law impact

**Spec-law change required.** Durable-terminal-state semantics, mutation-authority precedence (workflow vs projection), projection-source precedence, and reconciliation repair authority are product-observable contracts. Primary capability: `advance-workflow`.

**Bypass rationale:** none. RCA produced by `/adv-problem`, revised on workflow-history and terminal-path evidence, carried forward per rq-defectOriginRca01.

## Temporal Correctness Obligations

Design must satisfy all of these. Mechanisms are **not** chosen here — `/adv-discover` and `/adv-design` decide them. These are the correctness bar any solution is measured against.

- **O1 — Authority direction.** A workflow state transition must never be gated on a read of the projection derived from it. Idempotency must be grounded in workflow-owned evidence.
- **O2 — Durability is the workflow's responsibility.** Terminal state must be persisted through a retried Activity owned by the workflow, before it completes — not by caller-side best-effort. State required to outlive retention must not depend on workflow history surviving.
- **O3 — Correct primitive.** The terminal transition must use the right Temporal mechanism for graceful, handler-draining completion. `terminate()` (abrupt, skips drain and final writes) and `cancel()` (wrong semantics — cancellation is not archival) must be justified-or-rejected explicitly rather than reached for.
- **O4 — Completion proof, not acceptance proof.** Success must rest on evidence the transition was applied. Signal acceptance is not proof. Any read-based verification must account for Visibility eventual consistency with bounded backoff; a single immediate read is not proof.
- **O5 — Already-terminal is a first-class, correct outcome.** Re-archiving a completed workflow must be handled as legitimate idempotency evidence (e.g. `WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError`), not an error to swallow and not a reason to skip work.
- **O6 — No silent lossy flags.** Options such as `{ afterSuccess: false }` that disable durability or observability side effects must be explicit, justified, and covered by tests that fail if the disabled behavior is silently needed.

## What Changes

1. **Archive stops skipping its own transition on a projection read.** Idempotency re-grounded on workflow-owned evidence (O1, O5).
2. **The terminal path becomes durable.** Terminal state persisted via the workflow's retried Activity before completion, so it survives retention expiry (O2).
3. **The terminal transition uses the correct Temporal action**, with graceful completion and handler drain preserved (O3).
4. **Archive gains a real postcondition** proving the transition applied, not merely that a signal was accepted (O4).
5. **Projection ladder unified.** `adv_change_list` and `adv_change_show` resolve terminal status through one precedence order; `terminalFromWorkflow: 0` stops being a hardcoded lie.
6. **Repair/backfill path** for changes with a merged archive bundle on the default branch but no terminal state — including those whose workflow no longer exists.
7. **Reconciliation predicate fixed or scoped out with written rationale**; skip reasons observable in doctor output.
8. **`bulk_close` shares the corrected verifier**, since it shares the defective one.

## User Outcomes

- Archived work stays archived. It does not reappear as in-flight or get offered for re-archiving.
- When archive says it succeeded, it did. When it cannot confirm, it says so instead of claiming success.
- Retrying a partially-archived change actually finishes it, instead of silently skipping the step that was missed.
- Terminal status survives indefinitely, independent of how long Temporal retains history.
- The same change reports the same status everywhere in ADV.
- Already-broken changes get repaired rather than requiring manual cleanup, including ones whose Temporal history is long gone.
- `/adv-cleanup` stops producing false ready-to-archive candidates.
- Health diagnostics report state correctness, not just infrastructure liveness.

## Affected Code

- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:2108-2140` — `archiveChangeSignal` handler and its `afterSuccess: false`
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:2221-2245` — terminal path; missing durable write before return

- `plugin/src/tools/_recovery-writers.ts:108` — shared recovery-write path
- `plugin/src/archive/terminal-history.ts:411-416, 472` — hydration and projection precedence
- `plugin/src/temporal/reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:154, 161-165`, `reconcile-terminal-deps.ts:115-123, 171-172` — sweep predicate and candidacy

## Related Repositories

Single-repo change in `advance`. `pokeedge-web` is the cross-check subject only — **its state must not be modified by this change**.

## Constraints

- No `defineUpdate` in workflow-reachable code.
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` static import graph must not reach `storage/`, `tools/`, `tool-registry.ts`, `plugin-init.ts`, or `node:*`.
- Workflow changes must remain replay-deterministic; existing running workflows must not be broken by a non-replay-safe edit.
- Temporal integration tests are `.itest.ts`, routed through `src/temporal/__tests__/with-test-env.ts`.
- `pnpm run build:worker` before OOP Temporal integration tests.
- Verification must be end-to-end, not unit-only, and must include a retention-expiry (deleted-workflow) case.
- Repair must require positive terminal evidence. Absence of evidence must never complete a workflow.
- Re-grounding idempotency must not reintroduce duplicate-archive side effects (double bundle, double branch delete).

## Scope

### In Scope

- Archive precondition re-grounding — `statusAlreadyArchived` short-circuit (O1)
- Durable terminal persistence from the workflow before completion (O2)
- Correct terminal Temporal action with graceful drain (O3)
- Archive terminal postcondition — verify applied, not accepted (O4)
- Already-terminal handled as first-class idempotency evidence (O5)
- Audit of `afterSuccess: false` sites for silently-dropped durability (O6)

- Broader Temporal read-saturation/timeout work owned by `fixMultiSessionTemporalRead` and `fixArtifactReadFallback`
- General `/adv-cleanup` UX beyond removing false positives caused by this defect

### Must Not

- Must not raise retention or enable archival as the remedy
- Must not gate a workflow transition on a projection read
- Must not leave terminal durability as caller-side best-effort
- Must not complete a workflow on absence of evidence — only positive terminal evidence repairs
- Must not report success for an unverifiable postcondition
- Must not use `terminate()` or `cancel()` for archival without explicit written justification
- Must not introduce `defineUpdate`
- Must not treat a single immediate post-signal read as proof; Visibility is eventually consistent
- Must not break replay determinism for in-flight workflows
- Must not mutate `pokeedge-web`
- Must not mask the defect with a retry/fallback in place of the root-cause repair (P40)

ADV archive reports success on the strength of a Temporal signal being *accepted by the server*, never on the transition being *applied by the workflow*. No postcondition asserts the change workflow reached terminal state or that a new projection revision landed.

Consequences:
- Fully archived changes (bundle written, PR merged to default branch) keep reporting `status: draft`, `phase: release`, and resurface in `/adv-cleanup` as ready-to-archive candidates. Shipped work is offered for re-archiving.
- `adv_change_list` and `adv_change_show` disagree on the same change because they resolve terminal status from different projection sources.
- Terminal reconciliation inspects every candidate and repairs none, because its veto predicate reads the very projection the defect failed to update.
- Retention (24h TTL, archival disabled) then deletes the workflow, making the failure permanently unrecoverable and invisible.

Desired outcome: archive proves terminal state landed or reports failure; a backfill path repairs already-desynced changes including retention-expired ones; list and show agree; the reconciliation skip predicate is fixed or explicitly scoped out with rationale.

This is a mutation-durability defect, not an archive-only defect: `adv_change_bulk_close` shares the same postcondition verifier and exhibits the same symptom.

# Agreement — fixArchiveTerminalDurability

> Discovery completed 2026-08-04. All 9 agenda items resolved. Three proposal claims revised on evidence (see § Proposal Corrections).

## Objectives

1. **Archive stops skipping its own workflow transition.** Idempotency re-grounded on workflow-owned evidence rather than a disk-projection read (O1, O5).
2. **The workflow owns terminal durability.** Terminal state persisted via an awaited, retried Activity before the workflow returns, so it survives retention expiry (O2).
3. **Terminal transition uses natural completion** with handler drain preserved; `terminate()` and `cancel()` explicitly rejected on documented grounds (O3).
4. **Archive proves the transition applied**, not merely that a signal was accepted (O4).
5. **Projection ladder unified** across `adv_change_list` and `adv_change_show`; `terminalFromWorkflow: 0` stops being a hardcoded lie.
6. **Repair path** for changes with a merged archive bundle but no terminal state — including retention-expired workflows that reconciliation cannot currently reach.
7. **Reconciliation predicate fixed** and its skip reasons made observable.

## Discovery Findings (resolved agenda)

### D1 — Which path writes `status: "archived"` without signalling (agenda 1) — **RESOLVED, HIGH confidence**

Exactly one production producer fires the three archive signals: `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:1497` (`archiveConvergedSignal`), `:1505` (`archiveRequestedSignal`), `:1518` (`archiveChangeSignal`) — all inside `store.changes.save()`.

Three recovery writers stamp `status: "archived"` onto `changes/<id>/change.json` **without** signalling. The guard at `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:4877` then reads that projection, evaluates `statusAlreadyArchived === true`, and skips the only signal-firing call at `:4900`. Self-perpetuating.

Additionally, an early-return branch at `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:4481-4545` (`reconcileArchivedBundleRetry`) frequently wins before the guard is even reached, because the archive bundle is written independently. Either route yields: no archive signal ever reaches the workflow.

> Proposal cited `change.ts:4836-4838`; verified line numbers are `:4877` (guard) and `:4900` (save). Use the verified numbers.

### D2 — Correct terminal Temporal action (agenda 2) — **RESOLVED**

Natural completion. Documented shape:

1. Archive signal handler sets a `terminalRequested` flag and returns — it does **not** perform the external write itself.
2. Workflow main function: `await` the projection Activity → `await condition(allHandlersFinished)` → `return`.
3. Caller proves application via `handle.result()`, or `handle.describe()` (`status === COMPLETED`, expected `runId`) for the already-completed case.

`terminate()` **rejected**: runs no workflow code, no handler drain, no final write; closing event is `WorkflowExecutionTerminated`. `cancel()` **rejected**: cooperative-abort semantics, closing event `WorkflowExecutionCanceled` — cancellation is not archival.

`describe()` is authoritative for a single execution and bypasses Visibility. Visibility is eventually consistent with no published SLA and must never be used as proof.

### D3 — Why `afterSuccess: false` exists (agenda 3) — **RESOLVED**

Introduced in `6c68f0971b7963d4a4a2f4afab9cb893819188ac` (change `fixSignalHandlerThrow`, 2026-05-28). Intent: *the handler runs the success side-effects itself; the helper must not duplicate them.* At introduction each of the four call sites hand-wrote both `upsertSignalSearchAttributes` and its projection write, so the flag prevented double execution.

The archive handler subsequently retained the manual search-attribute upserts but lost the projection write. The flag is therefore not wrong in principle — it became a silent regression when the compensating write was dropped. Five current sites exist; all require audit under O6.

### D4 — Correct idempotency for archive (agenda 4) — **RESOLVED**

Idempotency moves from one global status short-circuit to per-side-effect guards plus workflow-owned evidence:

- **Transition idempotency** — ground on `handle.describe()`. A `WorkflowNotFoundError` from `signal()` is *ambiguous* (already-completed vs never-existed vs retention-deleted) and must be disambiguated by `describe()`, never treated as success on its own.
- **Side-effect idempotency** — duplicate bundle write and double branch delete are guarded individually (bundle-exists, branch-exists), not by suppressing the whole transition.

### D5 — Replay determinism (agenda 5) — **RESOLVED**

Adding an awaited Activity to the terminal path changes the command sequence and would break replay of in-flight executions. Rollout uses the three-step patching API: `patched('<id>')` → `deprecatePatch('<id>')` → remove. Continue-as-new rotation only removes the need where the archive can wait for the next rotation; it does not cover in-flight runs that must archive first. A replay test is required.

### D6 — Which reconciliation skip reason fires (agenda 6) — **RESOLVED, definitive**

`still_active`. For disk `draft` + merged bundle: `archived.has(id)` is true, but `isTerminalChangeStatus("draft")` is false so the change stays in the active set (`reconcile-terminal-deps.ts:66-68, 115-123`), and the veto at `reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:162-165` fires **before** the `no_archive_evidence` branch at `:167-170`.

Candidacy is additionally limited to `RUNNING` Visibility rows (`reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:154`), so retention-expired workflows are never enumerated at all — confirming they have no repair path via this sweep.

Skip reasons are dropped in two places: `plugin/src/tools/doctor.ts:1035` renders only a count, and `plugin-init.ts:675` captures the array into `lastTerminalReconcile` whose reader `getLastTerminalReconcile()` (`plugin-init.ts:650`) is never called by any production path.

### D7 — Durable terminal store of record (agenda 7) — **RESOLVED**

The Activity-written external projection is the store of record (`plugin/src/temporal/activities.ts:467-489`). The archive bundle remains corroborating evidence, required for repairing changes whose workflow is retention-expired. The ladder therefore stays multi-source but gains a single documented precedence order. Temporal's own guidance is explicit that history is not a system of record and that state outliving retention must be Activity-written to an external store.

### D8 — Shared-verifier blast radius (agenda 8) — **RESOLVED; proposal claim corrected**

~26 consumers enumerated. All but one handle `committed_unverified` / `recovered_unverified` correctly (mapping to `operator_required`, `state_unknown`, or throwing).

**The single genuine misleading-success consumer is `commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection` (`plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts:1114`)** — it returns `void`, so `committed_unverified` lands in a warn-only branch and the caller at `:554-561` never inspects it.

Two latent risks recorded but not misleading-success at their API surface: `persistStateToDisk` (`store-temporal/index.ts:278`) writes the file at `change-projection-transaction.ts:375-382` *before* verification, and `buildSummaryCommitProjection` (`store-temporal/shared.ts:505`) publishes the shard in an `afterCommit` hook at `change-summary-shard.ts:256-330` before an error can be reported.

### D9 — Sibling short-circuits (agenda 9) — **RESOLVED**

Release-gate `alreadyDone` guards (`archive-gate.ts:519-521, 1371-1372, 1717-1726`) share the *shape* but read workflow state via `changeStateQuery` (authoritative) — **not** the same defect class. The one structurally-equivalent recovery bypass is `saveRecoveredGateCompletion` (`archive-gate.ts:948-957`).

## Proposal Corrections

| Proposal claim | Discovery verdict |
|---|---|
| `bulk_close` shares the defective verifier (What Changes #8) | **Disproven.** `saveRecoveredStatusTransition` throws correctly (`_recovery-writers.ts:364, 389`). Replaced by the real consumer, `commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection`. |
| `WorkflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError` participates in idempotency (O5) | **Wrong SDK.** No such class in `sdk-typescript`; it is Cadence/Java. Re-grounded on `WorkflowNotFoundError` + `describe()` disambiguation. |
| Reconciliation skip reason unknown, `still_active` or `no_archive_evidence` (agenda 6) | **Resolved:** `still_active`, deterministically, by branch order. |
| Affected line `change.ts:4836-4838` | **Off by ~40 lines.** Verified: `:4877` guard, `:4900` save. |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — Archiving a change whose disk projection already reads `archived` still delivers the terminal transition to the workflow. Regression test covers the recovery-writer-then-archive sequence that produces the short-circuit today.
- **AC2** — The change workflow awaits a retried projection Activity before returning on the terminal path. Terminal state is readable from the external store after the workflow's history is gone.
- **AC3** — The terminal transition completes naturally with `allHandlersFinished` drained. No `terminate()` or `cancel()` on the archive path.
- **AC4** — Archive returns success only on evidence the transition was applied (`result()` / `describe()`), and returns an explicit unverified/failure outcome otherwise. Signal acceptance alone never yields success.
- **AC5** — Re-archiving an already-terminal workflow succeeds as idempotent, proven by `describe()`. `WorkflowNotFoundError` is never treated as success without disambiguation.
- **AC6** — `adv_change_list` and `adv_change_show` report the same status for a change with a merged archive bundle and a stale `draft` disk projection. Test asserts both surfaces together — no such test exists today.
- **AC7** — `terminalFromWorkflow` reflects a real count.
- **AC8** — A repair path restores terminal state for a change with a merged bundle and no terminal state, including when its workflow no longer exists. Repair acts only on positive evidence; absence of evidence never completes a workflow.
- **AC9** — The reconciliation predicate no longer vetoes a bundle-archived change on its stale disk status, and skip reasons (`changeId` + `reason`) are visible in doctor output.
- **AC10** — `commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection` surfaces `committed_unverified` to its caller instead of warning and continuing.
- **AC11** — All five `afterSuccess: false` sites audited; each is either justified in writing or given its compensating write, with a test that fails if a needed side-effect is silently dropped.
- **AC12** — Workflow-path edits are replay-safe for in-flight executions, demonstrated by a replay test.
- **AC13** — End-to-end verification includes a simulated retention-expiry (deleted-workflow) case.

## Constraints

- No `defineUpdate` in workflow-reachable code.
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` static import graph must not reach `storage/`, `tools/`, `tool-registry.ts`, `plugin-init.ts`, or `node:*`.
- Workflow edits must remain replay-deterministic; in-flight executions must not break.
- Temporal integration tests are `.itest.ts`, routed via `src/temporal/__tests__/with-test-env.ts`.
- `pnpm run build:worker` before OOP Temporal integration tests.
- Verification must be end-to-end, not unit-only.
- Repair requires positive terminal evidence.
- Re-grounded idempotency must not reintroduce duplicate bundle writes or double branch deletes.
- Spec deltas land in `.adv/specs/advance-workflow`.

## Avoidances

- Must not raise retention or enable archival as the remedy.
- Must not gate a workflow transition on a projection read.
- Must not leave terminal durability as caller-side best-effort.
- Must not complete a workflow on absence of evidence.
- Must not report success for an unverifiable postcondition.
- Must not use `terminate()` or `cancel()` for archival.
- Must not treat a single immediate read — or bare `WorkflowNotFoundError` — as proof.
- Must not break replay determinism for in-flight workflows.
- Must not mutate `pokeedge-web` state.
- Must not mask the defect with retry/fallback in place of root-cause repair (P40).

## Scope Adjustments from Discovery

**Added:** `commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection` misleading-success fix (AC10); making reconciliation skip reasons observable (AC9); `plugin-init.ts:650/675` dead-reader cleanup.

**Removed:** `adv_change_bulk_close` — disproven as a defect consumer.

**Recorded, not scoped:** `persistStateToDisk` write-before-verify and `buildSummaryCommitProjection` publish-before-error. Both are latent ordering risks, neither produces the reported symptom. Surface as follow-ups.

# Design — fixArchiveTerminalDurability

> Every mechanism below is cited at the **call site where it takes effect**, per P38. Line numbers verified against trunk at design time. Leverage scout run and integrated. Independent validation: **pass** (see § Validator Result). Production field evidence integrated (see § Field Evidence).

## Architecture Overview

The defect is one architectural inversion expressed in two places: **Temporal is treated as a side effect rather than as the authority.**

Today the archive flow does this:

```
caller reads disk projection → decides whether to transition the workflow
caller writes terminal state → workflow completes having written nothing durable
```

The design inverts both halves:

```
caller always requests the transition → workflow owns the decision
workflow awaits its own durable write → then drains handlers → then completes
caller proves completion from workflow evidence → then reports success
```

Three seams change:

| Seam | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Transition decision** (`change.ts:4877`) | disk read gates the signal | signal always sent; idempotency from workflow evidence |
| **Terminal durability** (`workflows.ts:2230-2240`) | nothing written; workflow returns | awaited projection Activity, then drain, then return |
| **Success proof** (`change.ts:4900` onward) | signal accepted ⇒ success | `describe()` proves `COMPLETED` ⇒ success |

Everything else in scope — ladder alignment, repair, reconciliation, the release-gate verifier — follows from making terminal state real and readable.

**Two passes materially reduced this design's footprint.** The leverage scout found four of five drafted mechanisms already had canonical implementations in-repo. Field evidence then showed the repair path (K6) also already exists and is merely mis-routed. The design now composes existing machinery almost throughout; the genuinely new surface is narrow: the awaited terminal write, and the explicit unconfigured-projection outcome.

## Field Evidence

Production data gathered during an `/adv-cleanup --execute` run on `advance`, 2026-08-04. Independently verified against source where load-bearing.

### F1 — AC8 has 10 real instances, and the refusal is circular

Ten changes are `status: "archived"` + `lifecycleState: "open"` + **no workflow**, unreachable by every tool:

`updateSubagentDispatch` · `fixValidationInputTimeout` · `hardenSlopScanTestEnv` · `runPokeedgeConsolidation` · `fixDeploymentSyncOrdering` · `addTypedOrchestrationApi` · `addLightweightChangeProfile` · `retireDeployWorkerBounce` · `fixTriageTimeouts` · `fixCrossProjectTrunkFirewall`

The refusal loop:

```
adv_archive_purge             → confirmed_failure — workflow not found for ID: adv/change/<pid>/<id>
adv_change_workflow_terminate → refused: change <id> is archived   (hint routes back to purge)
```

These become AC8's fixtures. They also convert AC8 from a hypothetical to a measured 10-instance backlog in this project alone.

### F2 — The convergence write AC8 needs already exists (verified)

`adv_change_workflow_terminate`'s `shipped_terminal` eligibility class already performs exactly the atomic write AC8 requires. Verified at `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:5454` (tool contract) and `:5960-6025` (classification and dispatch):

> `shipped_terminal` — describe shows RUNNING/PAUSED with no poison but the durable disk projection carries all 7 gates done + phase9_status done + a schema-valid archive bundle whose embedded `change.id` strictly equals the requested changeId; terminate + **atomic status/lifecycleState=archived convergence write** + read-after-write verification + two successor-race checks (pre-write + post-readback).

And the precondition that blocks it, same contract text:

> the change must exist and **NOT be archived** (archived changes route to `adv_archive_purge`, the sole archived-change lever — `rq-archivePurge01` semantics preserved)

So the mechanism is built, proof-gated, race-checked, and tested (`change.workflow-terminate.test.ts:832-1559`, `change/shipped-terminal-proof.test.ts`). It is unreachable for exactly the population that needs it, because the archived-change lever it defers to fails when the workflow is gone.

**This is a routing defect, not a missing capability.** K6 is re-scoped accordingly.

### F3 — The working half of the boundary

`adv_archive_purge` succeeds on archived + still-**running** workflow: 49/49 in one sweep, all with `includeDiskBundle: false`, every bundle preserved, verified 66 → 17 running workflows via `temporal workflow list`. Its archived-only guard also correctly refused all 17 genuinely-active changes (`not archived (status: draft)`) with zero mutations.

The repair surface works. It fails only when the workflow is already gone. **AC8 extends this path; it does not replace it.**

### F4 — AC6 and AC7 reproduce in the wild

**AC6:** `adv_change_list` reported `status: "draft"` for changes whose authoritative status is `archived`, because it enumerates by `lifecycleState` rather than `status`. This caused two wrong diagnoses in a single session before `adv_change_workflow_terminate`'s refusal exposed the truth. The consequence of L8's divergence is active misdiagnosis, not a cosmetic mismatch.

**AC7:** production `hydrationStats`:

```
{totalIds:214, fromMemo:2, fromCache:0, fromHydration:212,
 terminalCandidates:212, terminalFromArchive:75, terminalFromDisk:119,
 terminalFromWorkflow:0}
```

`terminalFromWorkflow: 0` confirmed in production. **Additionally verified:** `fromCache` is likewise a hardcoded literal — `const fromCache = 0;` at `storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:990`, asserted by `changes.test.ts:859`. It reports an absent feature as a measurement, the same honesty defect as `terminalFromWorkflow`. Folded into AC7's scope as an adjacent same-pattern fix (P25).

### F5 — Concrete trigger instance

`ensureTargetWorkers`, read post-archive:

```json
{"status":"archived", "lifecycleState":"open", "_source":"archive",
 "phase9_status":{"status":"failed",
   "error":"Unexpected error while making gRPC request"}}
```

A **transient** phase-9 gRPC failure produced **permanent** state corruption — no retry, no convergence. This is the predicted consequence of a terminal path that returns without a durable Activity write. Promoted to a required test case: *phase 9 fails after the bundle is written* (DDC11).

### F6 — Blast radius

- **Worktree cleanup is blocked by this bug.** `adv_worktree_delete` refuses with `INTEGRATION_REQUIRED` / `change_not_terminal`: *"Change `<id>` is unreachable; archive or close it before clearing the missing-from-disk registry entry."* Seven worktrees uncleanable until `lifecycleState` converges.
- Epic `advInfrastructureHealth`: 4 of 5 entries report `projection_missing`.
- Fleet scale: 299 leaked workflows across ~15 projects at peak (pokeedge 107, pokeedge-web 91).

### F7 — Explicitly NOT this change's scope

Read timeouts, `adv_doctor` false-healthy, and worker RSS belong to **#368**, not here. Note #368's original "uncached O(corpus) hydration" claim has been **retracted**; the cause is concurrent-session contention. This design does not inherit the retracted version and does not take that scope (see § Non-Scope).

### F8 — Tool-read contention explains observed flakiness

Four `advance` worker processes were live (374779, 446133, 488277, 698840); 374779 predates the current bundle and serves a stale generation. Reads against this change timed out at 10s under concurrency and succeeded when issued solo. This accounts for the `adv_change_show` timeouts encountered during design authoring — **not** change poisoning. No action here; recorded so it is not misdiagnosed later.

## Lever Citations

Each proposed mechanism traced from declaration to consuming call site.

### L1 — The transition guard (Fault 1)

**Call site:** `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:4877`

```ts
if (!dryRun && archiveResult.success) {
  const statusAlreadyArchived = change.status === "archived";
  if (!statusAlreadyArchived) {          // ← the lever
    ...
    await store.changes.save(change);    // :4900 — sole signal producer
```

`change.status` here is a **disk-projection read**. `store.changes.save()` at `:4900` is the only production producer of the three archive signals (`storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:1497`, `:1505`, `:1518`). Three recovery writers stamp `status: "archived"` onto disk without signalling; from then on `:4877` is permanently true and `:4900` is permanently skipped.

Confirmed no earlier stage preempts this lever: the guard sits inside the `archiveResult.success` branch, after release-gate completion and durable proof (`:4871-4874` ordering comment), so it is reached on every non-dry-run successful archive — except where the earlier `reconcileArchivedBundleRetry` early-return at `:4481-4545` short-circuits the whole block first. Validator confirmed that early-return branch conditions on `change.status === "archived" && existingBundlePath !== null`. **Both routes must be addressed**; fixing only `:4877` leaves the early-return path still silent (see K3 for the explicit mechanism).

### L2 — Terminal path with no durable write (Fault 2)

**Call site:** `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:2230-2240`

```ts
if (state.status === "archived" || state.status === "closed") {
  wf.log.info("workflow:completing", {...});   // :2231
  await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished);  // :2238
  return;                                      // :2239
}
```

Logs, drains, returns. **No projection write.** The wake predicate at `:2221-2225` fires on `state.status === "archived"`, which the archive handler sets via `archiveChangeInChangeState(state)` at `:2118`. So the workflow *does* complete — having durably recorded nothing.

Validator sharpened this: the archive handler at `:2108-2139` has **no projection call at all** — not even a fire-and-forget one — unlike `gateCompleted` at `:1754`, which does call `scheduleChangeProjection`. Archive is not a weakened case of the general pattern; it is an omitted one.

Note the predicate at `:2222` covers `"archived" || "closed"` — see K11.

### L3 — The projection write is fire-and-forget (deeper than proposal stated)

**Call site:** `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:1027-1036`

```ts
const scheduleChangeProjection = (signalName: string): void => {
  if (!projectionChangesDir) return;
  void projectChangeState(signalName).catch(...);   // :1029 — NOT awaited
};
```

`projectChangeState` (`:999-1025`) *does* await the `writeChangeProjection` Activity at `:1003`. But `scheduleChangeProjection` discards the promise at `:1029`.

**Consequence:** restoring the archive handler's projection write by flipping `afterSuccess`/`projectAfter` at `workflows.ts:2138` would **still not produce durability** — the Activity would be scheduled and then abandoned when the workflow returns at `:2239`. Once the workflow function returns, in-flight Activities are considered cancelled and not retried (Temporal TMPRL1102 semantics).

This is the decisive reason the fix must land in the **workflow main function**, not in the signal handler.

### L4 — Silent no-op when projection is unconfigured

**Call site:** `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:1000` — `if (!projectionChangesDir) return true;`

Returns `true` (success) when no projection directory is configured. A terminal path that trusts this return value would report durable success having written nothing. Must be distinguished from a real write.

### L5 — Release-gate verifier swallows `committed_unverified`

**Call site:** `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts:553-561`

```ts
if (!completionResult.recoveryMutation) {
  await commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection({...});   // :554 — returns void
}
```

`commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection` (`:1079-1135`) already computes `result.kind` at `:1131` — it simply logs and returns `void`, so the caller at `:554` cannot observe `committed_unverified`. Sole genuine misleading-success consumer of the shared verifier out of ~26 enumerated.

### L6 — Reconciliation veto ordering

**Call site:** `plugin/src/temporal/reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:162-165`

```ts
if (active.has(changeId)) {
  result.skipped.push({ changeId, reason: "still_active" });   // :163
  continue;
}
if (!archived.has(changeId)) {                                  // :167
  result.skipped.push({ changeId, reason: "no_archive_evidence" });
```

`active` is built from disk status (`reconcile-terminal-deps.ts:66-68, 115-123`), so a `draft` disk row keeps the change "active" even with a merged bundle present. The veto at `:162` runs **before** the evidence check at `:167` — `still_active` always wins. Candidacy is further gated at `:154` (`wf.status.name !== "RUNNING"`), so retention-expired workflows are never enumerated by `owner.list` at `:141-144`.

### L7 — Hardcoded hydration stats

**Call sites:** `plugin/src/archive/terminal-history.ts:472` — `terminalFromWorkflow: 0,` (literal inside the `hydrationStats` object returned at `:477-481`), and `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:990` — `const fromCache = 0;` (asserted by `changes.test.ts:859`).

Both report absent features as measurements. F4 confirms the first in production.

### L8 — Ladder divergence is ONE OPTION, not two resolvers

**Call sites:** `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:1604-1614` and `:2077-2089`.

Both `list` and `listSummary` call **the same** resolver, `readProjectionChangeList`. They differ by a single option:

```ts
// list() — :1611-1613
// Active list output still uses archive bundles to dominate stale
// active projections; routine status summaries do not need this.
loadArchiveForActiveShadow: true,

// listSummary() — :2077-2089
// (option absent)
```

`adv_change_show` resolves via `changes.get` → `readProjectionSnapshot`, which is archive-bundle-dominant (`store-temporal/index.ts:235, 237`).

So the divergence is not architectural — it is one deliberately-omitted flag whose justifying comment ("routine status summaries do not need this") is falsified by F4's production misdiagnosis. **No shared resolver needs to be built; one already exists.**

### L9 — The repair routing block

**Call site:** `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:5454` (eligibility contract) and `:5960-6025` (classification/dispatch).

`shipped_terminal` performs the convergence write; the not-archived precondition routes archived changes to `adv_archive_purge`; purge fails when no workflow exists. The lever is the precondition, not the write. See F2/K6.

## Key Decisions

### K1 — Durable terminal write lives in the workflow main function, awaited, before the drain

The terminal block at `workflows.ts:2230-2240` gains an **awaited** projection write:

```
terminal detected
  → await projectChangeState("terminal")     // awaited, not scheduled
  → await wf.condition(allHandlersFinished)  // drain
  → return
```

`projectChangeState` already awaits the retried `writeChangeProjection` Activity at `:1003`. **No new Activity is introduced** — the existing proxied Activity is finally used on the path that needs it most. Constraint C2 (workflows.ts import graph) is trivially satisfied: no new imports.

**Why BEFORE the drain, not after** *(validator flagged this as the design's most load-bearing choice; rationale recorded per its recommendation)*:

- **BEFORE-drain** — the drain runs *after* the Activity round-trip, so any signal that arrives *during* that round-trip is still caught and completed before return.
- **AFTER-drain** — `drain → await Activity → return` would leave a window in which signals arriving during the Activity await are abandoned when the workflow returns, producing TMPRL1102 unfinished-handler abandonment.

BEFORE-drain is therefore not merely acceptable but strictly safer. The one theoretical cost — a handler mutating state after the projection snapshot is taken — is bounded: terminal-status mutations are applied atomically before the first await within a single Workflow Task (`workflows.ts:1917`), so the snapshot passed to the Activity already carries `status=archived`, `release=done`, `phase9=done`. A late non-terminal mutation may miss this projection, but it is captured by the drain and is not terminal state.

`scheduleChangeProjection`'s fire-and-forget shape at `:1029` is **retained** for non-terminal signals — a deliberate latency choice, not the defect. The terminal path simply stops using it.

**Rejected:** writing inside the archive signal handler at `:2112-2137`. A handler is the wrong owner — an awaited Activity there yields control, letting the main function complete first; a fire-and-forget one is abandoned per TMPRL1102. Exactly the failure L3 describes.

### K2 — Unconfigured projection is an explicit outcome, never silent success

L4's `return true` at `:1000` is made distinguishable. The terminal path must know the difference between *wrote durably* and *had nowhere to write*. When no projection directory is configured, the workflow logs an explicit terminal-durability-unavailable signal and the caller's proof step treats the change as unverified rather than archived.

This keeps DONT4 (never complete on absence of evidence) and DONT5 (never report success for an unverifiable postcondition) honest in the degenerate configuration.

### K3 — Idempotency moves from one global guard to per-side-effect guards

The `statusAlreadyArchived` short-circuit at `change.ts:4877` is removed. In its place:

- **Transition idempotency** — the signal is always sent. Re-signalling a workflow that already reached terminal is safe: `archiveChangeInChangeState` is a state-setter, and a completed workflow rejects the signal, which K4 disambiguates.
- **Side-effect idempotency** — the two genuinely non-idempotent effects (bundle write, branch delete) are guarded *individually* at their own call sites (bundle-exists, branch-exists), satisfying C8.

**The `:4481-4545` early-return mechanism, stated explicitly** *(per validator note)*: that branch conditions on `change.status === "archived" && existingBundlePath !== null` and returns before reaching `:4877`. Removing the `:4877` guard alone therefore does **not** satisfy AC1 for changes taking this path. The early return must continue to skip *bundle re-writing* — which is correct and preserves C8 — while still performing the transition request and the K4 proof before returning. AC1's regression test must exercise the recovery-writer-then-archive sequence **through this path specifically**, not only through `:4877`.

This is the direct answer to O1/DONT2: the workflow transition stops being gated on the projection derived from it.

### K4 — Proof composes existing `boundedRetry` + canonical completion classifier

*(Scout candidate A — adopted.)*

Proof is `describe()`-based, never signal acceptance, never Visibility. Both halves exist and are composed rather than rewritten:

- **Bounded backoff** — `boundedRetry<T>` (`plugin/src/utils/fs.ts:70`, tested at `utils/fs.test.ts:60`): generic injectable exponential-backoff-with-jitter returning `{ok, value, attempts, elapsedMs}`. Supplies DDC3's bounded deadline directly.
- **Completion disambiguation** — `classifyMutationRecoveryDecision` (`plugin/src/tools/monotonic-recovery.ts:105-187`, probe-first path at `:157-186`) already implements the probe-first `describe()` decision tree, using the canonical completed-workflow classifier in `plugin/src/temporal/recovery-classification.ts` (`:14-15` regex constant; `:24` the `missing_workflow` mapping — corrected citation per validator).

**Evidence rules:**

- Primary proof: `handle.describe()` → `status === COMPLETED` with expected `runId`. Single-entity read, authoritative, bypasses Visibility.
- Bounded backoff, not a single immediate read (DONT7).
- Visibility List/Count is never proof — eventually consistent, no published SLA.
- `WorkflowNotFoundError` is ambiguous. Per `recovery-classification.ts:24`, `missing_workflow` **conflates completed and retention-expired**; they are indistinguishable at the describe() layer. The external projection (K5 precedence) is therefore the required tiebreaker (AC5, DONT7).

**Rejected — `handle.result()` as primary proof:** blocks the caller until close, and after retention expiry throws indistinguishably from "never existed". **Rejected — `terminate()`:** runs no workflow code, no handler drain, writes nothing. **Rejected — `cancel()`:** cooperative-abort; cancellation is not archival. Both satisfy DONT6/O3.

### K5 — Align one option; do not build a resolver

*(Revised by scout follow-up — the design's largest simplification.)*

Per L8, `readProjectionChangeList` **is** the shared resolver. The work reduces to:

1. Align `listSummary` (`changes.ts:2077-2089`) with `list` (`:1611-1613`) on archive-bundle dominance; correct the now-falsified comment.
2. Feed `terminalFromWorkflow` (`terminal-history.ts:472`) a real count.
3. **Adjacent same-pattern fix (P25):** `const fromCache = 0` (`changes.ts:990`) reports an absent feature as a measurement. Either report it honestly or remove the field; update `changes.test.ts:859` accordingly.

Precedence order, stated once:

```
1. external durable projection (Activity-written)   ← store of record
2. archive bundle on the default branch             ← corroborating evidence
3. disk projection                                  ← last resort
```

Kept multi-source deliberately: the bundle is the **only** evidence available for a retention-expired change whose workflow is gone — required by K6 and by K4's tiebreaker.

**F4 note:** `adv_change_list` enumerating by `lifecycleState` rather than `status` is part of this surface; AC6's "both surfaces agree" test must assert on the field triage actually reads.

**Accepted cost:** enabling archive-shadow loading adds bundle reads to the summary path, contradicting the intent of the comment at `:1611-1613`. Correctness wins — F4 shows the current behavior actively produced two wrong diagnoses. Budgeted in DDC5.

### K6 — Repair re-routes the existing convergence write; it does not build one

*(Scout candidate E + field evidence F1/F2/F3 — substantially re-scoped.)*

The original draft proposed a repair path routed through `recoveryAuthority` (`_recovery-writers.ts:63-95`) and `coordinateChangeMutation` → `commitChangeProjection` (`change-mutation-coordinator.ts:556-598`) per `rq-recoveryProjectionTransaction01`. That boundary requirement still holds. But F2 establishes the convergence write **already exists**, fully proof-gated and race-checked, in `adv_change_workflow_terminate`'s `shipped_terminal` class (`change.ts:5454`, `:5960-6025`).

The defect is **routing**, not capability:

```
archived + workflow running  → adv_archive_purge            ✓ works (49/49, F3)
archived + workflow gone     → adv_archive_purge            ✗ workflow not found
                             → adv_change_workflow_terminate ✗ refused: is archived
                                                              (hint → purge)   ← circular
```

K6 therefore **opens the existing lever to the stranded population** rather than adding a parallel writer:

- The `shipped_terminal` proof requirements are retained in full — all 7 gates done, `phase9_status` done, schema-valid bundle with strictly-equal embedded `change.id`, read-after-write verification, both successor-race checks. These *are* C7's positive-evidence gate; they must not be relaxed to reach the new population.
- The path must tolerate an absent workflow. For a retention-expired change there is nothing to terminate — the operation degrades to convergence-write-only, which is legitimate precisely because K5 makes the external projection the store of record.
- Absence of a workflow is **never** evidence of archival (C7, DONT4). Without a valid bundle, the change is reported indeterminate and left alone.
- `rq-archivePurge01` semantics are preserved; this does not make `adv_change_workflow_terminate` a general archived-change lever, only an evidence-gated repair for the no-workflow case that purge structurally cannot serve.

F1's ten changes are the acceptance fixtures. F3's 49/49 purge success defines the boundary not to regress.

### K7 — Reconciliation: evidence before veto

The branches at `reconcile-terminal-workflows.ts:162` and `:167` are reordered so positive bundle evidence is evaluated before the disk-derived `active` veto. The veto remains — it must, to protect genuinely active changes — but stops firing on a change whose only claim to being active is the stale projection this defect corrupts.

Skip reasons (`changeId` + `reason`) become observable: `doctor.ts:1035` renders rows rather than a bare count, and the dead reader `plugin-init.ts:650` (`getLastTerminalReconcile`, never called) is wired to that output or removed.

The `RUNNING`-only candidacy filter at `:154` stays — a retention-expired workflow genuinely cannot be reconciled by this sweep. Those changes are K6's responsibility; the handoff is documented rather than widening the sweep.

### K8 — Release-gate verifier reuses `mapCommitOutcome`

*(Scout candidate B — adopted.)*

`commitArchiveReleaseGateProjection` (`archive-gate.ts:1079-1135`) already computes `result.kind` at `:1131`. It changes from `void` to returning the **canonical** mapped outcome via `mapCommitOutcome` (`change-mutation-coordinator.ts:606-644`, `committed_unverified → recovered_unverified`), already consumed by ~25 callers through `MutationOutcome`. The caller at `:553-561` fails closed, matching `change-mutation-readiness-adapter.ts:65-121`.

**No new outcome type.** Validator confirmed this *repairs an existing `rq-recoveryProjectionTransaction01`.3 violation* and aligns with `rq-releaseProjectionDurability01`.2.

### K9 — `afterSuccess: false` audit, not blanket removal

The flag's original intent (commit `6c68f097`, change `fixSignalHandlerThrow`) was legitimate: *the handler runs the success side-effects itself; the helper must not duplicate them.* It became a regression only where the compensating write was later dropped — the archive handler at `:2136` retains the search-attribute upsert but not the projection write.

**Necessary but not sufficient** for archive — per L3, archive's durability comes from K1.

### K10 — Replay safety on existing, CI-enforced patch infrastructure

*(Scout candidate D — adopted.)*

`patched()` → `deprecatePatch()` → remove, on existing enforced infrastructure:

- `scripts/gen-replay-fixture.ts` generates sanitized histories.
- `plugin/src/temporal/__tests__/replay-determinism.test.ts:12` replays them; fixture format at `__tests__/replay/histories/*.metadata.json`.
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflow-evolution-guard.ts:1-16, 95-103` is a CI check that **blocks archive** unless a patch + fixture exist (`extractPatchMarkers`).
- Precedent in tree: `ARCHIVE_PROJECTION_RECONCILER_PATCH` (`workflows.ts:477-478`).
- Runbook: `docs/temporal-recovery.md:847-919`.

Step 2 is mechanical: generate a pre-patch history that completes via the current no-durable-write terminal branch, then replay current patched code through the legacy skip branch. **`op-name-vN` naming is mandatory** or the evolution guard blocks archive — machine-enforced, not stylistic.

Continue-as-new does not make this moot: a change archiving before its next rotation replays old history against new code (AC12/C3/DONT8).

### K11 — `closeChange` is covered; stated explicitly

*(Scout candidate C — adopted as scope clarification.)*

The wake predicate at `workflows.ts:2222` fires on `state.status === "archived" || "closed"`, and `closeChangeInChangeState` (`temporal/change-state.ts:3194-3311`) sets `status = "closed"` and routes through the **same** block at `:2230-2240`.

K1 therefore fixes close-path terminal durability retroactively. AC2's wording is status-agnostic, so close is within the approved contract, not new scope.

Recorded explicitly so implementation does not narrow the fix to an `archived`-only branch — which would leave `closed` silently broken and reintroduce the same defect class on the sibling path. Verification covers both statuses (DDC10).

## ADR Drafts

Two decisions meet the 3-criteria rubric (hard-to-reverse, surprising-without-context, real-tradeoff):

- **`docs/adr/NNNN-workflow-owns-terminal-durability.md`** — why terminal state is written by an awaited Activity inside the workflow rather than by the caller, and why the write precedes the handler drain. Hard to reverse (patching cost), surprising (the fire-and-forget helper looks like it already does this), genuine tradeoff (terminal-path latency vs durability; BEFORE- vs AFTER-drain handler safety).
- **`docs/adr/NNNN-describe-not-visibility-for-proof.md`** — why single-entity `describe()` with bounded backoff is the proof mechanism and Visibility never is, including the `missing_workflow` conflation that forces an external-projection tiebreaker. Surprising without context, real tradeoff.

**Why this is the long-term-correct shape rather than the minimal patch.**

The minimal patch is deleting the `statusAlreadyArchived` guard at `change.ts:4877`. It would make archive signal again — and would still produce no durable terminal state, because L3 shows the projection write is abandoned at `:1029` regardless. It would also miss the `:4481` early-return path entirely. The symptom would partially recede while the invariant stayed broken, resurfacing at the next retention expiry in a harder-to-diagnose form. That is precisely the masking DONT10/P40 forbids.

The chosen shape puts each responsibility with its owner:

- The **workflow** owns terminal durability — the only component that knows when it is terminal and the only one that can write before completing.
- The **caller** owns proof — the component reporting success to a user.
- The **projection** owns nothing authoritative — it becomes a derived read, which is what a projection is.

Three independent passes converged on *less new code, not more*. The scout resolved four of five mechanisms to canonical existing implementations. The K5 follow-up found the "shared resolver" already existed behind one flag. Field evidence then showed K6's repair write already existed behind one precondition. A design that keeps shrinking while satisfying the same 32-item contract is evidence the target shape is the one the codebase was already converging on.
